Pair recurrence across models and across bootstrap resamples

Source: R/pair_recurrence.R
pair_recurrence.Rd

A descriptive index of how often the same untreated partner is chosen, reported next to pair instability (1 minus the recurrence across models). The across-models and bootstrap versions are kept separate and are never mixed.

Usage

pair_recurrence(match_set, use_gate = TRUE, models = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'pair_recurrence'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

match_set

A match_set from match_each_model().

use_gate

TRUE (default) to use the models that passed the log-loss gate; FALSE to use every model. The bootstrap version does not depend on the gate.

models

Optional character vector of model ids to use instead of a gate; it overrides use_gate. The wrapper propensity_sensitivity() passes the final quality-gate set (log-loss and balance) this way.

x

A pair_recurrence object.

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class "pair_recurrence": a list with patients (one row per patient: row, id, treated, modal_control_models, pair_recurrence_models, modal_control_bootstrap, pair_recurrence_bootstrap, pair_recurrence_bootstrap_uncorrected; NA for untreated patients), summary (means over treated, floor_models, ceiling_models, ceiling_bootstrap, expected_ceiling_bootstrap_uncorrected, bootstrap_samples_used), models_used, quality_gate_left_fewer_than_two_models and settings.

Details

Across models. For treated patient i, the modal partner is the untreated partner chosen most often by the models in use; the recurrence is the share of those models choosing it (see the denominator rule below). Floor 1 / M (every model picks a different untreated partner), ceiling 1.

Across bootstrap resamples (when the match set has a bootstrap block: logistic regression only, so it measures sampling instability). The modal partner is taken over the resamples. The corrected recurrence divides the number of resamples in which i is matched to its modal partner by the number of resamples in which both i and that partner are present; its ceiling is 1. The uncorrected version divides by the number of resamples in which i is present; its expected ceiling is about 1 - 1/e = 0.632, because a given partner is missing from about 37 % of bootstrap samples. Skipped resamples are ignored.

Expect the across-models version near its floor whenever untreated patients are dense: the index measures crowding more than model dependence.

Tie rule and denominator rule

  • Ties. When two or more untreated partners are chosen equally often, the modal partner is the one that comes first in the data (smallest row position). The same rule is used across models and across bootstrap resamples. With three models that all choose different untreated partners, the recurrence is 1/3 whichever partner is called modal.

  • Denominator across models. The share is taken over the models in use that matched the patient. Without a caliper every model matches every treated patient, so the denominator is M, the number of models in use. With a caliper a model may leave a patient unmatched; that model is left out of the denominator, and a patient unmatched by every model gets NA. The reported floor is 1 / M.

  • Denominator across bootstrap resamples. Corrected: resamples in which both the patient and its modal partner are present. Uncorrected: resamples in which the patient is present. Skipped resamples are left out of both.

Quality gate

With use_gate = TRUE only the models that passed the log-loss gate are used. If fewer than two passed, all models are used and quality_gate_left_fewer_than_two_models is TRUE . The flag reports the gate's outcome whatever use_gate is.

Examples

data("lalonde", package = "MatchIt")
model_set <- fit_propensity_models(
  treat ~ age + educ + race + married + nodegree + re74 + re75,
  data = lalonde, seeds = 1, n_trees = 100,
  algorithms = c("logistic_regression", "random_forest", "gradient_boosting")
)
match_set <- match_each_model(model_set, lalonde, replace = TRUE, bootstrap_samples = 20)
recurrence <- pair_recurrence(match_set)
recurrence
#> Pair recurrence: 2 model(s) in use (after the log-loss gate)
#> Across models: mean over treated 0.5811 (floor 0.5, ceiling 1)
#> Across 20 bootstrap resamples: corrected 0.3119 (ceiling 1); uncorrected 0.2067 (expected ceiling 0.6321)
